findings.mechanism: A plated hole with no copper land either gets rejected/queried at fabrication or is plated anyway, reducing the finished hole diameter by roughly the plating thickness and leaving an unanchored barrel; for connector alignment pegs this risks peg interference fit changes and plating tear-out during connector press-in. The holes should be NPTH.
findings.reasoning: Confirmed directly in the saved board via pcbnew (PTH attribute, size==drill). This is a mechanical/manufacturing issue only (no net attached), so severity is minor, but it is a definite native-rule violation in the saved candidate.

findings.location: Polygonus-Universal-Base.kicad_pcb, GND zone on F.Cu; pads C15.2 (107.85,98.76), U7.4 (101.01,102.68), C14.2 (101.59,104.29) mm (VR module area)
findings.mechanism: A single-spoke thermal connection halves the intended copper cross-section at the joint: higher joint resistance/inductance on decoupling and comparator ground pins, and a mechanically/thermally weaker solder connection that is more vulnerable to spoke necking during fill changes or fabrication etch variation.
findings.reasoning: The pads remain electrically connected (DRC shows 0 unconnected items), so the impact is marginal rather than functional; but it violates the board's own fill constraints in the saved state, which the read-only review must take as-is. Minor defect.

findings.condition: The CAN2 bus internally links the ECU module (J2.73/74 at x≈144), both TJA1051T-3 wideband transceivers (U21 at x≈78, U20 at x≈178), and external connector pins J1.11/15 via a ~107 mm stub. The only termination resistors on the net — 120 Ω R36 at the U20 end and 120 Ω R37 at the U21 end — are both marked DNP ((dnp yes), in_bom no) in the saved design, so as-built the bus has zero ohmic termination; line loading is 2×47 pF per line (C29/C33, C30/C34) plus two NUP2105L clamps.

components R36/R37 dnp:true; nets /CAN2+ and /CAN2- node lists
footprint R36 dnp:true, pads on /CAN2+ and /CAN2-

findings.location: wbo-can-trans.kicad_sch (both instances /WBO-CAN-TRANS/ and /WBO-CAN-TRANS1/), R36/R37; board nets /CAN2+ and /CAN2-, R36 at (175.0,140.7), R37 at (81.6,140.6) mm
findings.mechanism: An unterminated high-speed CAN bus has no defined recessive differential load: reflections and slow recessive transitions cause bit errors, and the README-advertised internal wideband function (wideband controllers 'connected internally to CAN bus #2') then depends entirely on termination existing inside the plug-in brain module or in the external harness, neither of which is part of this donor. Conversely, if a builder populates both R36 and R37 and also attaches an externally terminated CAN2 harness through J1.11/15, the bus load falls to ~40 Ω, below the transceiver's normal 50–65 Ω operating load.
findings.reasoning: Placement of the two terminators at the physical bus ends is correct and the DNP pattern may be a deliberate configuration option, so this is not provable as a defect from the donor alone. But the packet scope explicitly claims 'internal dual-wideband CAN termination', and the saved evidence shows no termination is actually populated: correct operation of an advertised core feature rests on an unverified assumption about the module or harness. Major concern requiring documentation or module-side verification.
findings.title: Internal dual-wideband CAN2 bus has no populated termination: both 120 Ω terminators (R36, R37) are DNP

findings.condition: Each wideband sensor heater return is a single 0.6 mm wide, 35 µm thick B.Cu track with no parallel copper and no plane relief: measured R ≈ 92 mΩ (/HeaterNeg) and ≈ 129 mΩ (/HeaterNeg2). IPC-2221 external estimate for 0.6 mm/1 oz is ≈1.65 A at 10 °C rise; at the ~2.5 A LSU heater warm-up current the estimated rise is ≈26 °C (≈39 °C at 3 A) with 0.57–0.81 W dissipated along the trace and 0.23–0.32 V dropped in the heater low side.

evidence.locator: section 4 'Heater returns' — pcbnew segment listing, resistance and IPC-2221 calculations with assumptions
nets /HeaterNeg (J1.108, U1.11, U1.12) and /HeaterNeg2 (J1.76, U2.11, U2.12)
0.6 mm B.Cu segments on /HeaterNeg and /HeaterNeg2

findings.location: Polygonus-Universal-Base.kicad_pcb, nets /HeaterNeg (J1.108 → U1.11/12, ≈112 mm, B.Cu) and /HeaterNeg2 (J1.76 → U2.11/12, ≈158 mm, B.Cu)
findings.mechanism: During every cold start the heater PWM ramp drives ~2–2.5 A through these traces for tens of seconds to minutes; in an engine-bay ambient the added 25–40 °C self-heating pushes local trace temperature well above the surrounding board, stressing laminate and solder joints over life, and the series drop slightly reduces heater voltage authority available to the module's closed-loop heater control.
findings.reasoning: Width alone does not establish a failure — heater current is duty-limited and the estimates are chart fits, so this is a concern, not a defect. It is the thinnest sustained-current copper on the board relative to its expected load and merits either a width increase, paralleled layers, or a documented thermal justification.
findings.title: Wideband heater return currents carried on single 0.6 mm tracks up to 158 mm long

findings.condition: The fused 12 V rail is distributed on the In.Power.Cu plane, but the entire net has just three 0.4 mm vias. The ETB1 driver (U15, TLE9201SG, 6 A-class with internal current limit above 6 A) is fed exclusively through a 0.8 mm wide, 4.6 mm long 1 oz F.Cu segment into the J1.73/74 pin barrels; the ETB2 driver (U3) is fed through the three-via group (≈2.3 A each at 10 °C rise estimate, ≈7 A combined).

evidence.locator: section 4 'ETB H-bridge supply' — full track/via/pad extraction and IPC-2221 calculations

findings.location: Polygonus-Universal-Base.kicad_pcb, net /12V_MR_FUSE: U15 pad 4 (120.54,44.91) via 0.8 mm×4.6 mm F.Cu neck to J1.73/74 barrels; U3 pad 4 (103.68,45.1) via 0.8 mm×1.6 mm neck and the net's only 3 vias (0.4 mm drill) at (109–111.2,52.5) mm
findings.mechanism: At nominal throttle currents (1–2 A) the 0.8 mm neck sits near 10 °C rise — acceptable. During motor stall or driver current-limit events (>6 A), IPC-2221 extrapolation puts the 0.8 mm segment above 100 °C rise if sustained; repeated limit/thermal-shutdown cycling of the TLE9201 can hold average current high while the trace, unlike the IC, has no protection. The three-via group for ETB2 is adequate only if current shares evenly and events stay brief.
findings.reasoning: Short necks tolerate brief overloads and throttle stall events are transient, so no defect is provable; but a 6 A-class bridge fed through a single 0.8 mm neck and a net served by three small vias is marginal by estimate and worth widening or paralleling. Reported as a calculated concern, not a thermal disqualification.
findings.title: ETB H-bridge supply pads reach the 12V_MR_FUSE plane through narrow necks and only three 0.4 mm vias net-wide

findings.mechanism: The design builds only from the caches embedded in the schematic and board files; a clean checkout cannot re-resolve, diff, or update these footprints/symbols against sources, so library drift (such as the already-present J2 footprint substitution) cannot be audited, and any footprint refresh in KiCad would fail or silently diverge.

No electrical impact in the saved state since caches are intact — minor defect in manufacturing-data/reproducibility hygiene.

findings.location: Polygonus-Universal-Base.kicad_sch root sheet: #PWR01 GND pin (36.8,78.7); A1 pin 8 VMOT (48.3,219.7); J2 pin 90 12V_IGN (293.4,174.0); A1 pin 2 ~FLT (38.1,224.8); J2 pins 40/41 5V_SENSOR_1 (262.9,128.3/130.8)
findings.mechanism: These rails are genuinely fed from the vehicle harness through J1 (12V_KEY: J1.45↔J2.90; 12V_MR_FUSE carries F1 output), so the undriven-pin errors reflect missing PWR_FLAG markers rather than missing supplies; the pin_to_pin error reflects the J2 module symbol modelling its paralleled 5V output pins both as Power output; A1 ~FLT is an open fault output (netlist: unconnected-(A1-~FLT-Pad2)) lacking an NC flag. None indicates a physical copper fault, but unresolved errors mask any future real ERC regressions.
findings.reasoning: Evidence-supported native errors in the saved schematic; root-cause analysis shows schematic-modelling hygiene (missing PWR_FLAG/NC markers, symbol pin typing) rather than electrical faults, hence info severity. Left at defect because the native rule set is violated as saved and the errors should be resolved or waived explicitly.
findings.title: Five native ERC errors remain: undriven power-input pins, unmarked NC pin, and paralleled power-output pins

limitations: Zone fills evaluated as saved; the read-only candidate forbids a refill pass, so fill-dependent results (starved thermals, connectivity) reflect the saved state only.

Ampacity figures are IPC-2221 chart-fit estimates at assumed 35 µm copper and still air; no IPC-2152 lookup, FEA, or measured thermal data — they bound marginality but do not qualify or disqualify the design thermally.
Molex 64333-0100 terminal and Keystone 3568 fuse-clip current ratings were not verified against manufacturer data; connector-pin ampacity is not assessed.
TLE9201SG current-limit and LSU heater current figures are from reviewer knowledge, not freshly retrieved datasheets, and are stated as assumptions in the experiments notes.
Internal construction of the Polygonus brain module and wideband modules (including any on-module CAN termination) is outside the donor and could not be verified.
No EMC, automotive transient, ignition-energy, or wideband control-stability analysis (declared out of scope by the packet).
Whether 'Simon' / 'hellen-one-common' libraries resolve via the original author's global library tables cannot be determined from the candidate.
